chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them)

He was asked about a man who had a slave girl, and his wife annoyed him regarding her, so he said: 'She is a charity upon you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he said that for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, let him fulfill it; and if he did not say it (for Allah), then it is for him to retract if he wishes regarding her.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband revoke a gift of a slave girl to his wife if it was not given as a formal charity for Allah?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi distinguishes between a gift given for Allah's sake (sadaqah li-llah), which becomes irrevocable, and a simple marital gift, which remains revocable at the giver's discretion. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the critical role of intention (niyyah) in determining the legal status of property transfers within the family structure. The hadith clarifies that the spiritual weight of the gift dictates its permanence, offering practical guidance for resolving domestic disputes over property.
